content.title: Narrowing: Prove What You Have
content.context:
```ts
type Value = string | number;
```

Inside a function that receives a `Value`, TypeScript cannot assume it is a string or a number until your code gives it evidence.

That process is called **narrowing**.
goals: Use conditions that narrow a union to a more specific type before performing type-specific work.

content.title: Repair it
Why narrowing matters
content.text:
Without narrowing, your code is making an unsupported assumption.

With narrowing, your code says:

**“I know there are multiple possibilities. I checked which one I have. Now this operation is safe for that case.”**

That is a powerful engineering pattern far beyond TypeScript.

options.text: Evidence that lets code and the type checker work with a more specific possibility.
A way to avoid writing any conditions.
A way to convert every value into a string.

feedback.correct: Narrowing is the bridge from “could be several things” to “in this branch, we have this specific thing.”
feedback.incorrect: Narrowing is the bridge from “could be several things” to “in this branch, we have this specific thing.”
